title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Patient Financial Services Terms: Hardship Applications and the Ship-Time Past-Due Measure
content:
# Hardship applications in the past-due measure for a plan member waiver

Patient Financial Services Terms, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, Larkfield Medical Supply.

These terms govern how a posting named on a hardship application is treated in the program's past-due amount when Larkfield counts the units of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that a plan member waiver covers for the next delivery on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment. A hardship application concerns one posting on the program's billing record; the application read is the latest hardship application logged on the program.

## Scope of the ship-time past-due test

For the ship-time past-due test of the refill count for a delivery drawing on the grant resting on the newest written order and of the plan member waiver count, and only for that test, a posting counts as past due once the whole calendar months given by the tier's past-due age in days divided by 30, rounded down, have passed from its posting date to today, no posting counts on a tier whose past-due age is 0 days, the past-due remittance patient responsibility, other than a posting named on a hardship application, counts as covered while an approved payment plan's installments are current, and a posting named on a hardship application is set aside as the hardship rules of these terms state; every program hold for a past-due balance still rests on the program hold rule, under which, on tiers whose past-due age is greater than 0 days, the program's past-due amount is at least the tier's past-due hold minimum and no approved payment plan covers it.

## The set-aside

The hardship adjustment takes a posting under a hardship application off the past-due amount, by these rules:

1. When the latest hardship application on the program names a posting and is still awaiting decision, that posting's amount is taken off.
2. When it is approved, that posting's amount less the balance adjustments posted against it is taken off.
3. Otherwise nothing is taken off.

## Status table

| Status of the latest hardship application | Amount taken off the past-due amount |
|---|---|
| awaiting decision | the full amount of the posting it names |
| approved | the amount of the posting it names, less the balance adjustments posted against that posting |
| denied, completed or withdrawn | nothing |
| no hardship application on the program | nothing |

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- A hypothetical hardship application names a remittance patient responsibility posting of 120.00 USD and is awaiting decision: 120.00 is taken off.
- The same application, approved, with a balance adjustment of 45.00 posted against that posting: 75.00 is taken off.
- The same application, denied: nothing is taken off, and the posting counts in the past-due amount like any other.
- An older application was approved but a later application, logged afterwards, is withdrawn: the later one is the latest, so nothing is taken off.
